Authentic Use of
 Software & Technology
in an Applied Statistics Course
 Damian W. Betebenner, Yun Xiang, & Xiaohui Yue

 Department of Educational Research, Measurement, and Evaluation
 Lynch School of Education, Boston College

Perspectives & Purpose
• Background of computer use in curriculum
 development
• Difference between inauthentic use and
 authentic use of technology (cognitive tool)
• The central purpose: to authentically
 incorporate the use of technology in an
 applied statistics class.

Frameworks for the Implementation of
 Technology
• Definition of “authentic”
 Following Hennessy & Murphy (1999), an activity is authentic if
 it is:
 1. coherent and personally meaningful, and
 2. purposeful within a social framework—the ordinary practices
 of culture. (critical)

• Such a critique of expert knowledge aligns well
 with a large number of learning theories
• Chicken-egg dilemma emerges when attempting to
 situate technology use within expert practice

The Goal of the Study
• By illuminating what we think are best practice
 considerations for the implementation of
 technology into an applied statistics classroom,
 we hope to help educators from any discipline
 interrogate their own (in)authentic use of
 technology.

Setting & Methodology (i)
• Many of the implementations of technology
 in the classroom lacking due to a lack of
 authenticity
• Major challenge with regard to the seamless
 integration of computer software use with
 the development of theory in the class
• Limitations of the lecture/lab class format
• An attempt to overcome the limitation

Setting & Methodology (ii)
• An authentic use of software requires an operating
 computer in the classroom that is projected in such
 as way so that all students can view the process as
 it takes place
• The limitation of PowerPoint: This distance between
 “the pointer” and “the voice”
• Our solution to this dilemma: instead of projecting
 the software onto a basic reflective surface, the
 GUI is projected onto a touch sensitive white board
 (TSWB)
• Advantages of TSWB

Setting & Methodology (iii)
• Critical reflection of practice through participant
 observation
• The setting for the participant observations
 occurred at two different universities:
 In 5 classes where a TSWB was made available
 and
 in 6 classes without a TSWB.
 Classes were no larger than 35 students
• How was TSWB used in class?

Results & Conclusions (i)
 --Advantages of TSWB
A separate lab is no longer needed to demonstrate
 software use
• When devising lesson plans/lectures, our focus resides on
 investigating rich problems in class out of which theory and
 software use flows.
• Compared with separate lab sections to introduce students to
 computer use, the TSWB allowed the instructor to better
 coordinate computer use.
• Whereas teaching a computer lab can be analogous to “herding
 cats”, having a central projected computer allows one to proceed
 through the analysis at a measured pace that the students can
 follow.
• The ideal situation was for the students to have computers with
 which they can follow along (e.g., laptops, high speed wireless,
 and adequate deskspace). The students didn’t feel compelled to
 write down the mouse strokes one must follow to perform the
 analyses.

Results & Conclusions (ii)
Richer and less contrived examples can be explored
• In an investigation of regression, for example, with a
 working computer available a scatterplot depicting
 hundreds, if not thousands, of data points is easily
 available. Moreover, so is the depiction of the regression
 line together with coefficients for its representation as a
 linear equation.

• Richer examples, ideally, lead to more student involvement.
 Having a computer handy allows the instructor to follow
 through on analyses for such questions. The only limitation
 is the instructors expertise.

Results & Conclusions (iii)

Students are exposed to an authentic discussion of
 theory and application
• The instructor’s discussion is a refined
 encapsulation of the manner in which experts
 engage statistics. Thus, the instructor’s model
 expert practice for the students.

• Many questions from students can immediately
 and meaningfully be investigated using the
 software in front of the students. Such
 investigations acculturate the students in a manner
 consistent with that employed by expert.

Results & Conclusions (iv)
• Other advantages
• Limitations of TSWB

Future of the Study
• The future of authentic instruction that incorporates technology/
 software lies with the interface between the technology/software and
 the subject matter which, in turn, is brought to life through the
 instructor’s fluency with that technology/software.
• In situations where technology/software has yet to find an essential
 niche within a discipline (or instructors are not fluent with its use) the
 result is usually inauthentic instruction relying upon highly contrived
 exercises.
• The key to authentic incorporation of technology in the classroom lies
 with the answer to the question:
 How do/would/should I, an expert, utilize technology in my own discipline
 specific research?
 Once this question is answered, the trick is to transfer this enact this
 utilization of technology in the classroom and engage students in that
 process. Undoubtedly, this not a simple endeavor.
